readings.title: Shamgar's Deliverance
readings.subtitle: The Ox Goad
readings.text: [Judges 3:31] And after him was Shamgar son of Anath, and he struck <dn>את</dn> six hundred men of the Philistines with an ox goad. And he too saved <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: Deborah and Barak
readings.subtitle: The Defeat of Sisera
readings.text: [Judges 4:1] And when Ěhuḏ was dead, the children of Yisra’ěl again did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [2] Therefore <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sold them into the hand of Yaḇin the sovereign of Kena‛an, who reigned in Ḥatsor. And the commander of his army was Sisera, who was dwelling in Ḥarosheth Haggoyim. [3] And the children of Yisra’ěl cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, because he had nine hundred chariots of iron, and for twenty years he harshly oppressed <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl. [4] And Deḇorah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappiḏoth, was ruling <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl at that time. [5] And she was dwelling under the palm tree of Deḇorah between Ramah and Běyth Ěl in the mountains of Ephrayim. And the children of Yisra’ěl came up to her for right-ruling. [6] And she sent and called for Baraq son of Aḇino‛am from Qeḏesh in Naphtali, and said to him, “Has not <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl commanded, <dq>‘Go, and you shall draw towards Mount Taḇor, and shall take with you ten thousand men of the sons of Naphtali and of the sons of Zeḇulun,</dq> [7] <dq>and <dn>I</dn> shall draw unto you <dn>את</dn> Sisera, the commander of Yaḇin’s army, with his chariots and <dn>את</dn> his company at the wadi Qishon, and shall give him into your hand’</dq>?” [8] And Baraq said to her, “If you go with me, then I shall go; but if you do not go with me, I do not go.” [9] And she said, “I shall certainly go with you. Only, there shall be no esteem for you in the journey you are taking, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is going to sell <dn>את</dn> Sisera into the hand of a woman.” So Deḇorah arose and went with Baraq to Qeḏesh. [10] And Baraq called <dn>את</dn> Zeḇulun and <dn>את</dn> Naphtali to Qeḏesh. And he went up – ten thousand men under his command – and Deḇorah went up with him. [11] And Ḥeḇer the Qěynite, of the children of Ḥoḇaḇ the father-in-law of Mosheh, had separated himself from the Qěynites and pitched his tent near the terebinth tree at Tsa‛anayim, which is beside Qeḏesh. [12] And they reported to Sisera that Baraq son of Aḇino‛am had gone up to Mount Taḇor. [13] So Sisera called <dn>את</dn> all his chariots, nine hundred chariots of iron, and <dn>את</dn> all the people who were with him, from Ḥarosheth Haggoyim to the wadi Qishon. [14] And Deḇorah said to Baraq, “Rise up! For this is the day in which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given <dn>את</dn> Sisera into your hand. Has not <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gone out before you?” And Baraq went down from Mount Taḇor with ten thousand men after him. [15] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> destroyed <dn>את</dn> Sisera and <dn>את</dn> all his chariots and <dn>את</dn> all his army with the edge of the sword before Baraq. And Sisera leaped from his chariot and fled away on foot. [16] But Baraq pursued the chariots and the army as far as Ḥarosheth Haggoyim, and all the army of Sisera fell by the edge of the sword, not one was left. [17] Sisera, meanwhile, had fled on foot to the tent of Ya‛ěl, the wife of Ḥeḇer the Qěynite, for there was peace between Yaḇin sovereign of Ḥatsor and the house of Ḥeḇer the Qěynite. [18] And Ya‛ěl went out to meet Sisera, and said to him, “Turn aside, my master, turn aside to me, do not fear.” So he turned aside with her into the tent, and she covered him with a blanket. [19] And he said to her, “Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty.” So she opened <dn>את</dn> a bottle of milk, and gave him a drink, and covered him. [20] And he said to her, “Stand at the door of the tent, and it shall be if anyone comes and asks you, and says, ‘Is there a man here?’ you shall say, ‘No.’ ” [21] But Ya‛ěl, Ḥeḇer’s wife, took <dn>את</dn> a tent peg and took <dn>את</dn> a hammer in her hand, and went softly to him and drove <dn>את</dn> the peg into the side of his head, and it went down into the ground – for he was fast asleep and exhausted – and he died. [22] And see, as Baraq pursued <dn>את</dn> Sisera, Ya‛ěl came out to meet him, and said to him, “Come, let me show you <dn>את</dn> the man whom you are seeking.” And when he went into her tent, there lay Sisera, dead with the peg in the side of his head. [23] And on that day <dn>Elohim</dn> humbled <dn>את</dn> Yaḇin sovereign of Kena‛an in the presence of the children of Yisra’ěl. [24] And the hand of the children of Yisra’ěl grew stronger and stronger against Yaḇin sovereign of Kena‛an, until they had cut off <dn>את</dn> Yaḇin sovereign of Kena‛an.

readings.title: The Song of Deborah
readings.subtitle: A Hymn of Victory
readings.text: [Judges 5:1] And on that day Deḇorah and Baraq son of Aḇino‛am sang, saying, [2] “For leaders leading in Yisra’ěl, for the people volunteering, bless <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! [3] “Hear, O sovereigns! Give ear, O princes! I, I do sing to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>; I sing praise to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl. [4] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, when <dn>You</dn> went out from Sě‛ir, when <dn>You</dn> stepped from the field of Eḏom, the earth shook and the heavens poured, the clouds also poured water. [5] “The mountains flowed at the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, this Sinai, at the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl. [6] “In the days of Shamgar, the son of Anath, in the days of Ya‛ěl, the highways were deserted, and the travellers went in crooked ways. [7] “Leadership ceased, it ceased in Yisra’ěl, until I, Deḇorah, arose – a mother in Yisra’ěl arose. [8] “They chose new mighty ones, then fighting was in the gates! Neither a shield nor spear was seen among forty thousand in Yisra’ěl. [9] “My heart is towards the inscribers of Yisra’ěl, the volunteers among the people. Bless <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! [10] “You who ride on white donkeys, you who sit on rich carpets, and you who walk along the way, declare it! [11] “By the voice of shouters, between the places of drawing water, there they recount the righteous acts of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the righteous acts of <dn>His</dn> leadership in Yisra’ěl; then the people of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall go down to the gates. [12] “Wake up, wake up, Deḇorah! Wake up, wake up, sing a song! Arise, Baraq, and lead your captives away, O son of Aḇino‛am! [13] “Then <dn>He</dn> set the remnant to rule the nobles; <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came down for me against the mighty ones. [14] “Out of Ephrayim their root is against Amalěq. After you, Binyamin, with your peoples, out of Maḵir inscribers came down, and out of Zeḇulun those who handle the scribe’s reed. [15] “And the heads of Yissasḵar were with Deḇorah. And as Yissasḵar, so was Baraq sent into the valley under his command. Among the divisions of Re’uḇěn there were great searchings of heart. [16] “Why did you remain among the sheepfolds, to hear the bleatings of the flocks? The divisions of Re’uḇěn have great searchings of heart. [17] “Gil‛aḏ remained beyond the Yarděn, and why did Dan remain on ships? Ashěr continued at the seashore, and remained by its landing places. [18] “Zeḇulun is a people who risked their lives to the point of death, Naphtali also, on the heights of the field. [19] “Sovereigns came, they fought, then the sovereigns of Kena‛an fought in Ta‛anaḵ, by the waters of Meḡiddo; they took no spoils of silver. [20] “From the heavens they fought; the stars from their courses fought against Sisera. [21] “The wadi of Qishon swept them away, that age-old wadi, the wadi of Qishon. O my being, you have trampled in strength! [22] “Then stamped hoofs of horses, with the galloping, galloping of his steeds. [23] Curse Měroz,’ said a messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘curse, curse its inhabitants, because they did not come to the help of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to the help of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> among the mighty.’ [24] “Blessed above women is Ya‛ěl, the wife of Ḥeḇer the Qěynite – above women in tents she is blessed. [25] “He asked for water, she gave milk; she brought out curdled milk in a bowl for nobles. [26] “She stretched her hand to the tent peg, and her right hand to the workmen’s hammer. Then she pounded Sisera, she smashed his head, she pierced and struck through the side of his head. [27] “Between her feet he bowed, he fell, he lay still; between her feet he bowed, he fell; where he bowed, there he fell – destroyed. [28] “Through the window the mother of Sisera looked, and cried out through the lattice, ‘Why does his chariot delay to come? Why have the steps of his chariots tarried?’ [29] “The wise ones of her princesses answered her, indeed, she answered herself, [30] Do they not find and divide the spoil: a girl or two for each man; a spoil of dyed work for Sisera, a spoil of dyed work embroidered, dyed work richly embroidered for the necks of the looter?’ [31] “So do all <dn>Your</dn> enemies perish, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! But let those who love <dn>Him</dn> be like the sun rising in its might!” And the land had rest forty years.

readings.title: The Call of Gideon
readings.subtitle: The Fleece and the Altar
readings.text: [Judges 6:1] And the children of Yisra’ěl did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave them into the hand of Miḏyan for seven years, [2] and the hand of Miḏyan was strong against Yisra’ěl. And before the faces of the Miḏyanites the children of Yisra’ěl made for themselves <dn>את</dn> the refuges which are in the mountains, and <dn>את</dn> the caves, and <dn>את</dn> the strongholds. [3] And it came to be, whenever Yisra’ěl had sown, that Miḏyan would come up, and Amalěq and the people of the East would come up against them, [4] and encamp against them and destroy <dn>את</dn> the increase of the soil as far as Azzah, and leave no food in Yisra’ěl, neither sheep nor ox nor donkey. [5] For they came up with their livestock and their tents, coming in as numerous as locusts. And they and their camels were without number. And they came into the land to destroy it. [6] Thus Yisra’ěl was brought very low because of Miḏyan, and the children of Yisra’ěl cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [7] And it came to be, when the children of Yisra’ěl cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> because of Miḏyan, [8] that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent a prophet to the children of Yisra’ěl, who said to them, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> have brought <dn>את</dn> you up from Mitsrayim and <dn>I</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> you out of the house of bondage,</dq> [9] <dq>and <dn>I</dn> delivered <dn>את</dn> you out of the hand of the Mitsrites and out of the hand of all your oppressors, and drove <dn>את</dn> them out before you and gave you <dn>את</dn> their land.</dq> [10] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> said to you, “<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, do not fear <dn>את</dn> the mighty ones of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell. And you have not obeyed <dn>My</dn> voice.” ’</dq> ” [11] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came and sat under the terebinth tree which was in Ophrah, which belonged to Yo’ash the Aḇi‛ezerite, while his son Giḏ‛on threshed wheat in the winepress, to hide it from the eyes of the Miḏyanites. [12] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to him, and said to him, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with you, you mighty brave one!” [13] And Giḏ‛on said to <dn>Him</dn>, “O my master, if <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with us, why has all this come upon us? And where are all <dn>His</dn> wonders which our fathers related to us, saying, ‘Did not <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> bring us up from Mitsrayim?’ But now <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has left us and given us into the hands of Miḏyan.” [14] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> turned to him and said, <dq>“Go in this strength of yours, and you shall save <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl from the hand of the Miḏyanites. Have <dn>I</dn> not sent you?”</dq> [15] And he said to <dn>Him</dn>, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, with what do I save <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl? See, my clan is the weakest in Menashsheh, and I am the least in my father’s house.” [16] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Because <dn>I</dn> am with you, you shall strike <dn>את</dn> the Miḏyanites as one man.”</dq> [17] And he said to <dn>Him</dn>, “Please, if I have found favour in <dn>Your</dn> eyes, then show me a sign that it is <dn>You</dn> who are speaking with me. [18] “Please do not move away from here, until I come to <dn>You</dn> and bring out <dn>את</dn> my offering and set it before <dn>You</dn>.” And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall stay until you return.”</dq> [19] And Giḏ‛on went in, and prepared a young goat, and unleavened bread from an ěphah of flour. <dn>את</dn> The meat he put in a basket, and <dn>את</dn> the broth he put in a pot. And he brought them out to <dn>Him</dn>, under the terebinth tree, and presented it. [20] And the Messenger of <dn>Elohim</dn> said to him, “Take <dn>את</dn> the meat and <dn>את</dn> the unleavened bread and lay them on this rock, and pour out <dn>את</dn> the broth.” And he did so. [21] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> put forth <dn>את</dn> the end of the staff that was in <dn>His</dn> hand, and touched the meat and the unleavened bread. And fire went up out of the rock and consumed <dn>את</dn> the meat and <dn>את</dn> the unleavened bread. And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> went from his sight. [22] And when Giḏ‛on saw that <dn>He</dn> was a Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, Giḏ‛on said, “Oh Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! For I have seen a Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> face to face.” [23] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Peace be with you! Do not fear, you do not die.”</dq> [24] And Giḏ‛on built a slaughter-place there to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and called it: <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> Shalom. To this day it is still in Ophrah of the Aḇi‛ezerites. [25] And the same night it came to be that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Take <dn>את</dn> the young bull of your father, and <dn>את</dn> the second bull of seven years old, and you shall throw down <dn>את</dn> the slaughter-place of Ba‛al that your father has, and cut down <dn>את</dn> the Ashěrah that is beside it.</dq> [26] <dq>“And you shall build a slaughter-place to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> on top of this rock in an orderly way, and shall take <dn>את</dn> the second bull and offer an ascending offering with the wood of the image which you cut down.”</dq> [27] And Giḏ‛on took ten men from among his servants and did as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had said to him. And it came to be, because he feared <dn>את</dn> his father’s household and <dn>את</dn> the men of the city too much to do it by day, that he did it by night. [28] And the men of the city arose early in the morning and saw the slaughter-place of Ba‛al was broken down, and <dn>את</dn> the Ashěrah that was beside it had been cut down, and <dn>את</dn> the second bull was being offered on the slaughter-place which was built. [29] And they said to each other, “Who has done this deed?” And when they had inquired and asked, they said, “Giḏ‛on son of Yo’ash has done <dn>את</dn> this deed.” [30] And the men of the city said to Yo’ash, “Bring out <dn>את</dn> your son, so that he dies, for he has broken down <dn>את</dn> the slaughter-place of Ba‛al, and because he has cut down <dn>את</dn> the Ashěrah that was beside it.” [31] And Yo’ash said to all who stood against him, “You, would you plead for Ba‛al? You, would you save <dn>את</dn> him? Let the one who would plead for him be put to death by morning! If he is a mighty one, let him plead for himself, because his slaughter-place has been broken down!” [32] So that day he called him Yerubba‛al, saying, “Let Ba‛al plead against him, because he has broken down <dn>את</dn> his slaughter-place.” [33] Now all Miḏyan and Amalěq and the people of the East, were gathered together. And they passed over and encamped in the Valley of Yizre‛ěl. [34] Then the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came upon Giḏ‛on, and he blew the shophar, and the Aḇi‛ezerites gathered behind him. [35] And he sent messengers throughout all Menashsheh, who also gathered behind him. And he sent messengers to Ashěr, and to Zeḇulun, and to Naphtali. And they came up to meet them. [36] And Giḏ‛on said to <dn>Elohim</dn>, “If <dn>You</dn> are saving <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl by my hand as <dn>You</dn> have said, [37] see, I am placing <dn>את</dn> a fleece of wool on the threshing-floor. If there is dew only on the fleece, and it is dry on all the ground, then I shall know that <dn>You</dn> are saving <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl by my hand, as <dn>You</dn> have said.” [38] And it was so, and he rose early the next morning and pressed <dn>את</dn> the fleece, and wrung dew out of the fleece, to fill a bowl with water. [39] And Giḏ‛on said to <dn>Elohim</dn>, “Do not be displeased with me, and let me speak only this time: Please let me try only this time with the fleece, please let it be dry only on the fleece, and let there be dew on all the ground.” [40] And <dn>Elohim</dn> did so that night, and it was dry on the fleece only, but there was dew on all the ground.
